CHARACTER SHEET — HALLOWEEN BUNNY, CLEAN, ONE-PIECE WITH BUBBLE SKIRT (3-PANEL)
ATTACH: <<<image_1>>>

WHAT THIS IMAGE IS
A character sheet built EXACTLY LIKE THE REFERENCE SHEET: one single wide image on a plain mid-grey seamless studio background, divided into THREE PANELS SIDE BY SIDE, same layout, same framing, same scale of figure, same even studio light as <<<image_1>>>.
LEFT PANEL — the girl head to toe, FRONT view, standing straight, arms relaxed at her sides, feet together, looking into the lens.
CENTRE PANEL — the same girl head to toe, BACK view, standing the same way, so the ears, the full length of hair, the back of the garment and the tail all read clearly.
RIGHT PANEL — a HEAD-AND-SHOULDERS close-up, front, showing the ears, the face, the make-up and the top of the garment.
Only the clothing and the make-up are different from the reference sheet. The layout, the backdrop, the lighting and the presentation are the same.

ACTIVE REFERENCE
<<<image_1>>> — THE GIRL, THE SKIRT SHAPE AND THE SHEET FORMAT. The face, the hair and the body are 100% hers and must match exactly: the same facial features, the same soft round face shape, the same large dark eyes, the same full lips, the same slim build, the same height and the same proportions. THE HAIR IS IDENTICAL TO THE REFERENCE: long ash-light-brown hair falling past the chest, loose soft waves through the lengths, a full straight fringe sitting just above the eyebrows. THE SKIRT SILHOUETTE IS ALSO TAKEN FROM THIS REFERENCE — the same puffed bubble shape as the light blue gingham skirt she is wearing in it, rebuilt in the fabric and colour described below. The grey background, the three-panel layout and the soft catalogue lighting come from this reference too. Everything else about the clothing is replaced by the costume described below.

THE FABRIC — SPARKLE, BUT NOT SEQUINS
The dress and the ears headband are made of the same material: WHITE FABRIC DENSELY SCATTERED WITH TINY GLASS MICRO-CRYSTALS — a fine dusting of minute rhinestone grains sitting right in the surface of the cloth, like crushed diamond dust or frost. It throws small, sharp, pin-point sparkles where the light hits it and reads as clean white in the shadows. The grains are TINY AND IRREGULARLY SCATTERED so the surface stays smooth and continuous. THERE ARE NO ROUND SEQUIN DISCS, no rows, no grid, no overlapping scales, no beads and no large stones anywhere — only the fine crystal dust.

THE COSTUME — A ONE-PIECE HALLOWEEN BUNNY DRESS IN WHITE
IT IS A SINGLE GARMENT. The costume is ONE CONTINUOUS FITTED MINI DRESS running from the chest down into a puffed skirt — there is NO SEPARATE TOP, NO SHORTS, no visible waist seam, no band and no belt. The crystal-dusted white cloth runs unbroken from the neckline over the ribs and the waist and then gathers out into the skirt.
THE NECKLINE — straight across the collarbones, with TWO BROAD SHOULDER STRAPS about four centimetres wide and a fully closed back. A band of soft white marabou fluff trims the neckline.
THE BODICE — fitted close and smooth through the torso and down to the hip line, following the shape of the garment without wrinkling.

THE SKIRT — A SHORT PUFFED BUBBLE SKIRT, exactly the silhouette of the light blue gingham skirt in <<<image_1>>>. It is gathered softly into the hip line, BALLOONS OUTWARD AWAY FROM THE LEGS with real volume and a cushion of air inside, reaching its WIDEST POINT AROUND MID-THIGH, and then CURVES BACK IN UNDERNEATH ITSELF at the bottom, because THE HEM IS GATHERED AND TURNED UNDER AND STITCHED TO AN INNER LINING. That construction gives the skirt a SMOOTH, FULL, ROUNDED LOWER EDGE — a soft dome shape with a curved profile all the way round, never a flat hanging hem and never a straight A-line. Seen from the front, the outline of the skirt swells out from the hips and rounds back in at the bottom. Soft vertical gathers ripple over the surface. The hem finishes at MID-THIGH, even all the way round.
A BAND OF SOFT WHITE MARABOU FLUFF SITS RIGHT ON THAT ROUNDED HEM EDGE, about seven centimetres deep, following the curve the whole way round and matching the fluff at the neckline. Underneath, matching white under-shorts in the same fabric give full coverage, so from behind the skirt reads clean and modest.

EARS — a headband on top of the head covered in THE SAME WHITE MICRO-CRYSTAL FABRIC so the band itself sparkles, carrying two tall upright bunny ears about twenty-five centimetres high. The outer face of each ear is the same crystal-dusted white fabric, edged with soft white marabou fluff, and THE INNER PANEL OF EACH EAR IS PALE BABY PINK SATIN. The ears stand straight up with a gentle natural bend near the tip. The fringe sits neatly underneath the headband.

TAIL — a large round pom of fluffy white marabou, about twelve centimetres across, fixed at the centre back of the skirt on the fullest part of the puff. Clearly visible in the back panel.

WRIST CUFFS — a band of CLEAN WHITE marabou fluff around each wrist, about eight centimetres deep, worn on bare forearms.

BOOTS — WHITE BOOTS ENDING JUST BELOW THE KNEE, close-fitting and elegant. Smooth white stretch leather moulded snug to the calf, the top opening finishing a few centimetres BELOW THE KNEECAP. A BAND OF SOFT WHITE MARABOU FLUFF RUNS AROUND THE TOP OPENING OF EACH BOOT, about seven centimetres deep. A slender covered stiletto heel about nine centimetres high and a neat almond toe. Both boots identical.
The skin is bare between the hem of the skirt and the top of the boots.

NO JEWELLERY — the throat, wrists, ears and fingers are bare.

THE MAKE-UP — STRONG BUT RESTRAINED
Dewy, wet-looking skin with a real glow across the cheekbones, the nose and the brow bone. A SOFT ROSE-RED WASH on the eyelids and along the lower lash line, blended lightly out onto the top of the cheekbones and whispered across the bridge of the nose. THE BLUSH IS MODERATE — a gentle flush that shapes the eyes and cheeks rather than heavy saturated coverage; the natural skin tone still reads clearly through it and the colour stops well before the jaw and the temples. Long, strongly defined lashes top and bottom, each lash separated. Soft brushed-up brows kept light. Glossy, wet, deep rose lips. A scattering of small natural freckles across the nose and the tops of the cheeks. Nails short with a milky pale pink polish.
Nothing is stuck to the face — no rhinestones, no gems, no glitter particles, no stickers. The make-up is paint only.

EVERYTHING IS CLEAN
HER SKIN IS FLAWLESS AND EVEN-TONED EVERYWHERE — one continuous clear complexion across the forehead, both cheeks, the nose, the chin, the neck, both shoulders, both arms and both hands. The costume is BRAND NEW AND SPOTLESS: the crystal-dusted white cloth is an even clean white over the whole dress, and all the marabou fluff — the neckline, the skirt hem, both wrist cuffs, the ears and the tail — is pure fresh white with every filament clean. The boots are clean white leather. This is a costume she has just put on and has not worn anywhere yet.

POSE AND EXPRESSION
Front panel — standing tall and relaxed, shoulders square to camera, arms hanging easy at the sides with fingers softly open, feet together. Calm, level, unbothered expression, lips closed, looking straight down the lens.
Back panel — the same stance seen from directly behind, head facing away from camera, so the ears, the hair, the closed back of the bodice, the full rounded puff of the skirt and the pom tail all read clearly.
Close-up panel — head and shoulders, square to camera, chin level, same calm expression, both ears fully inside the frame with space above them, the make-up clearly readable.

BACKGROUND AND LIGHT
Plain mid-grey seamless studio paper behind all three panels, completely smooth and even, with a soft falloff to slightly darker grey at the outer edges — matching the reference sheet. Large soft frontal key with a broad fill, gentle wraparound shadow on the face, a soft contact shadow under the boots. The crystal dust throws fine pin-point sparkles. Skin tone natural and even, with no false shadow or highlight anywhere that could read as a mark. No colour cast on the backdrop.

OPTICS
85mm-equivalent look, about a 29° diagonal field of view, camera at chest height for the two full-length panels and at eye height for the close-up, straight on with no tilt. Everything sharp front to back, catalogue style.

QUALITY
High-resolution commercial lookbook photography. Real texture — the fine glint of the crystal dust in the weave, the individual filaments of the marabou fluff, the grain of the boot leather, the weave of the cloth. Natural skin texture with visible pores and real freckles, no plastic smoothing. Hands anatomically correct with five fingers. Arms and legs symmetrical and correctly proportioned. Crisp clean edges against the grey.

POSITIVE CONSTRAINTS
THE OUTPUT IS THE SAME KIND OF SHEET AS THE REFERENCE — one wide image, three panels: full-length front, full-length back, head-and-shoulders close-up, equally lit, equally scaled, on the same plain grey background.
THE FACE, THE HAIR COLOUR, THE HAIR LENGTH AND THE FRINGE ARE EXACTLY THOSE OF <<<image_1>>> IN ALL THREE PANELS, and it is clearly the same person in each.
HER SKIN IS COMPLETELY CLEAN AND EVEN IN EVERY PANEL — face, neck, shoulders, arms and hands are one clear unbroken complexion.
THE WHOLE COSTUME IS CLEAN AND NEW — an even white dress, pure white fluff at the neckline, hem, cuffs, ears and tail, and clean white boots.
THE SKIRT IS A PUFFED BUBBLE SKIRT WITH A ROUNDED LOWER EDGE — gathered at the hip, ballooning out away from the legs, widest at mid-thigh, and curving back in underneath itself at the bottom because the hem is gathered and turned under onto a lining. IT IS THE SAME BUBBLE SILHOUETTE AS THE LIGHT BLUE GINGHAM SKIRT IN <<<image_1>>>. It is not a flat hanging skirt and not a straight A-line.
A BAND OF WHITE MARABOU FLUFF SITS ON THAT ROUNDED HEM EDGE all the way round, matching the neckline, the wrist cuffs and the boot tops.
THE COSTUME IS ONE SINGLE CONTINUOUS DRESS — fitted bodice gathering into the puffed skirt in one piece, with no waist seam, no band and no separate top. Matching under-shorts beneath give full coverage.
THE DRESS AND THE EARS HEADBAND ARE WHITE FABRIC DUSTED WITH TINY GLASS MICRO-CRYSTALS — fine sharp sparkle, smooth continuous surface, with no round sequin discs, no rows and no large stones.
THE BOOTS END JUST BELOW THE KNEE — close-fitting white leather with the marabou band at the top opening and a slim high heel, identical on both legs.
THE BLUSH IS MODERATE — a soft rose flush on the eyelids, lower lash line and upper cheekbones, with the natural skin tone still reading through. Lashes long and defined, lips glossy deep rose, freckles natural, skin dewy. Nothing stuck to the face.
THERE IS NO JEWELLERY ANYWHERE.
THE THREE PANELS FILL THE FRAME with no large empty area anywhere.
The background is plain grey studio paper and contains nothing else — no props, no furniture, no text, no logos and no lettering of any kind.

CHARACTER SHEET — HALLOWEEN HORSE MASK (5-PANEL)
No reference images. Build the character entirely from the description below.

WHAT THIS IMAGE IS
A character sheet on a plain off-white seamless studio background with soft even catalogue lighting, laid out as FIVE PANELS SIDE BY SIDE in one wide image:
PANEL 1 — full length, FRONT view, horse mask ON, standing straight, feet shoulder-width apart, hands relaxed at his sides.
PANEL 2 — full length, SIDE PROFILE facing screen-left, horse mask ON, so the long muzzle and the depth of the mask read in profile.
PANEL 3 — full length, BACK view, horse mask ON, so the back of the mask, the mane and the back of the outfit read clearly.
PANEL 4 — a PORTRAIT, head and shoulders, front, THE MASK IS OFF and held down at his side out of frame, so we see HIS ACTUAL FACE AND HAIR clearly.
PANEL 5 — a CLOSE-UP of the horse mask worn, head and shoulders, front, showing the full detail of the mask.
All five panels share the same off-white backdrop, the same light and the same figure scale. In panels 4 and 5 the WHOLE HEAD FITS INSIDE THE FRAME with a clear band of empty background above it and the neck and shoulders visible below.

THE CHARACTER — AN ORIGINAL KOREAN TEEN BOY
A slim, tall Korean boy of about eighteen with an easy, slightly aloof presence.
FACE — pale clear skin with a natural matte finish, an oval face with a soft jawline and a defined chin, high flat cheekbones, straight dark low-set brows, warm dark brown almond eyes with a soft double eyelid, a straight narrow nose with a rounded tip, and a full, slightly pouted mouth with a clear cupid's bow. One small silver hoop in his left ear. No make-up beyond clean skin.
HAIR — black, mid-length and layered, with a soft textured fringe falling in separated pieces across the forehead down to the eyebrows, longer pieces framing the cheeks in front of the ears, and the back layered down to the nape. Natural soft wave, slightly messy, matte rather than shiny.
BUILD — slim and lean with narrow shoulders and long legs, about 180 cm, relaxed posture.

THE COSTUME — A NOVELTY HORSE MASK WORN WITH ORDINARY CLOTHES

THE MASK — a FULL-HEAD LATEX NOVELTY HORSE MASK of the classic kind, covering the entire head and neck. A long tan-brown horse face with a WIDE WHITE BLAZE running from between the ears down the front of the muzzle, a soft PINK MUZZLE with flared nostrils, big glossy dark brown eyes set at the sides with cream around them, two upright ears lined in pale pink, and A SHORT COARSE BLACK MANE standing up along the top of the head and running down the back of the neck. The mouth is slightly open in a blank, absurd grin showing big flat cream-coloured teeth. The latex has a soft matte sheen with visible moulded texture and a slightly heavy, rubbery hang at the base of the neck where it sits over his shoulders. It is deliberately silly and cheap-looking in the best way — a real shop-bought party mask, not a realistic animal head.

THE SHIRT — a short-sleeved camp-collar shirt in a SMALL LIGHT PLAID: fine criss-crossing lines of tan, warm brown, cream and a thin rust thread on a sandy beige ground. Boxy and relaxed through the body, worn fully buttoned but loose, the short sleeves falling just above the elbow with a soft turned cuff at the edge. The collar sits open and flat. The hem hangs loose over the waistband, untucked.
THE TIE — a narrow tie in THE SAME PLAID FABRIC as the shirt, knotted loosely at the throat with the knot pulled down a few centimetres so the collar sits open above it. It hangs straight down the front of the shirt.

THE TROUSERS — relaxed straight-cut trousers in a MUTED DARK TEAL-GREEN soft cotton, slightly loose through the thigh with a gentle taper, a flat front, a plain waistband, and the hem breaking once over the top of the shoe. Matte fabric with a soft natural drape and a few easy creases at the knee and ankle.

THE SHOES — CLASSIC LOW-TOP RED CANVAS SNEAKERS: bright red cotton canvas uppers, a WHITE RUBBER TOE CAP, a white rubber foxing stripe around the midsole, a cream rubber outsole and flat WHITE LACES threaded through metal eyelets. Worn and slightly creased across the toe box. Both identical. Completely plain with no badges, no patches, no stars, no printed marks and no lettering anywhere on them.

NO OTHER ACCESSORIES — no hat, no bag, no belt showing, no jewellery beyond the single small silver hoop in his left ear, nothing in his hands except the mask in panel 4.

POSE AND EXPRESSION
Panel 1 — standing straight and relaxed, shoulders square to camera, feet shoulder-width apart, arms hanging loose at his sides, the horse head facing straight down the lens. The absurd calm of a person wearing a horse mask and doing nothing about it.
Panel 2 — the same stance from the side, the mask facing screen-left so the long muzzle reads in full profile.
Panel 3 — the same stance from directly behind, so the mane, the back of the latex neck, the back of the shirt and the trousers read clearly.
Panel 4 — head and shoulders, front, MASK OFF, his own face visible, chin level, a calm neutral expression with the mouth closed, looking straight down the lens, the hair falling as described. The top edge of the latex mask is just visible at the very bottom corner of the frame where he holds it at his side.
Panel 5 — head and shoulders, MASK ON, square to camera, the full face of the horse filling the upper frame with the plaid collar and tie visible below.

BACKGROUND AND LIGHT
Plain off-white seamless studio paper behind all five panels, completely smooth and even, with a soft falloff to slightly darker at the outer edges. Large soft frontal key with a broad fill, gentle wraparound shadow, a soft contact shadow under the shoes. The latex catches a soft diffuse sheen across the muzzle and forehead; the plaid cotton reads matte with a visible weave; the canvas reads flat and slightly textured. Skin tone natural and even in panel 4. No colour cast on the backdrop.

OPTICS
85mm-equivalent look, about a 29° diagonal field of view, camera at chest height for the three full-length panels and at eye height for the two close panels, straight on with no tilt. Everything sharp front to back, catalogue style.

QUALITY
High-resolution commercial lookbook photography. Real texture — the moulded rubber grain and seam line of the latex mask, the coarse bristle of the mane, the cotton weave and crisp printed lines of the plaid, the woven canvas and rubber of the sneakers. Natural skin texture with visible pores in panel 4, no plastic smoothing. Hands anatomically correct with five fingers. Shoulders level, arms and legs correctly proportioned, both legs the same length and thickness. Crisp clean edges against the off-white.

POSITIVE CONSTRAINTS
FIVE PANELS IN ONE WIDE IMAGE — three full-length views with the mask on (front, side profile, back), one portrait with the mask off showing his real face, and one close-up with the mask on. Equally lit, equally scaled, on the same plain off-white background.
IT IS THE SAME PERSON AND THE SAME OUTFIT IN ALL FIVE PANELS.
THE MASK IS A FULL-HEAD TAN LATEX NOVELTY HORSE MASK with a white blaze, pink muzzle, upright ears, big flat teeth and a short black mane — covering the whole head and neck in panels 1, 2, 3 and 5.
IN PANEL 4 THE MASK IS OFF and his own face and hair are fully visible, with the whole head inside the frame.
THE TOP IS A SHORT-SLEEVED TAN-AND-BROWN PLAID SHIRT, fully buttoned and untucked, with A NARROW TIE IN THE SAME PLAID knotted loosely at the throat.
THE TROUSERS ARE MUTED DARK TEAL-GREEN, relaxed and straight, breaking over the shoes. They are a different fabric and colour from the shirt.
THE SHOES ARE RED LOW-TOP CANVAS SNEAKERS with a white rubber toe cap, white laces and a cream sole, identical on both feet and completely free of any badge, logo or lettering.
HE WEARS NO HAT AND NO BAG, and his hands are empty.
THE FIVE PANELS FILL THE FRAME with no large empty area anywhere.
